name: OR-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by six points and Hoyle is the incumbent
Hoyle has a large fundraising edge over DeSpain
Prediction markets price Hoyle's win probability at 94%
No public general-election polling in the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Hoyle: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a better than two-to-one fundraising advantage, with markets pricing her near certain to win. With no polls available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals, trimmed slightly toward the market's 94% pricing.
model.watch: Any late polling showing DeSpain competitive, or a surge of outside spending against Hoyle, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Val Hoyle seeks a third term in a southwestern Oregon district that leans Democratic by about six points. She enters the general election with a clear financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.2 million to Monique DeSpain's $680,000, and holds more cash on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly to support her, with no recorded opposition spending. DeSpain, a first-time candidate, has not attracted measurable outside backing. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have listed the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets put Hoyle's chances around 94%. The combination of a favorable district, an established incumbent, and a fundraising edge makes Hoyle a strong favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the final margin.
